system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 0. How to read the Seller's package

The package is built to discourage review. It says positions are "[STANDARD]", "cleared by both sides", "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened", and asks us to look only at "[OPEN]" items. **None of the items are marked [OPEN]**, so if we followed that note we would review nothing.

Those labels are the Seller's own characterisation. They are not agreements. I have reviewed every position on its merits. **Action:** please confirm internally whether Wattlebridge principals actually agreed any of these points. Unless they did, we should say in our cover note that nothing is agreed until the full SPA is agreed, and that the [STANDARD] labels are not accepted.

The "market context" paragraph is also advocacy, not fact. Some figures, such as a basket around 1% and an 18-month general limitation period, fall within a negotiable range. But the market treats these as limits on **general warranty claims only**. The draft quietly extends them to title, tax, fraud, specific indemnities and known issues, and that is not market.

The Disclosure Letter itself is useful to us. Read honestly, it confirms that several significant issues are **unresolved**. Each one is discussed below.

---

## 1. The limitation package (Clauses 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 General cap: 20% (AUD 4.8m), Clause 12.1
- 20% is at the lower end for a share sale of this size without W&I insurance. **Push for 30–50%**, or accept around 20% only if all three conditions in this section are met.
- Condition 1: fundamental warranties, tax and the specific indemnities sit **outside** the cap.
- Condition 2: W&I insurance is put in place, and the Seller funds or shares the premium.
- Condition 3: there is an escrow or retention (see section 6).

### 1.2 De minimis AUD 25,000 and basket AUD 250,000 (deductible), Clause 12.2
- The basket is about 1.04% of price. The real problem is that it operates as a **deductible**, with only the excess recoverable. **Push for a tipping basket** (once the threshold is reached, recovery runs from the first dollar), or a lower threshold of about 0.5% (AUD 120k).
- De minimis: **push to AUD 5–10k.** Also require that **related or series claims aggregate** for de minimis purposes. Otherwise a systemic issue such as data incidents or contract leakage can be split below the threshold.
- Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims, or to fraud.

### 1.3 Time limits, Clause 12.3 / 13: "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- 18 months for general warranties is acceptable. Ideally ask for 24 months, so that at least two audit cycles are covered.
- **Reject the "all Claims" default.** It would put title, tax and indemnity claims on an 18-month clock. Our proposed periods:
  - **Title/capacity:** 7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
  - **Tax:** at least the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, commonly 5–7 years. Unlimited for fraud or evasion.
  - **Specific indemnities:** tailored periods. For example, privacy should run long enough to cover regulatory action.

### 1.4 Fundamental/title warranties under the same cap and time limits
**Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing. The market position is:
- cap at **100% of price**;
- no thresholds;
- long survival.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature", Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Reject as drafted.** We need express carve-outs from all limitations for:
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives;
- specific indemnities, the tax indemnity and fundamental warranties, which should have their own regime;
- covenant and leakage breaches, and completion obligations.

The non-reliance clause should not be capable of excluding liability for the Seller's fraud. We should preserve our position on misleading or deceptive conduct as far as possible, at minimum for the Seller's written disclosures and replies to DD questions.

---

## 2. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

The Letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the whole data room and in public registers. **Reject.**

**Our position:**
- Only **specific disclosures** in the Letter qualify the warranties. They must be fairly disclosed, meaning with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and **financial effect** of the matter.
- The data room can be deemed disclosed only to the extent it is specifically cross-referenced in the Letter, against the relevant warranty.
- Public register disclosure should be limited to defined searches (ASIC and PPSR) on defined dates, with the results provided to us.
- **Specific indemnities are not qualified by disclosure.** That is the whole point of them.
- **Timing:** the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November. If warranties are repeated at Completion, the Seller should not be able to "update" disclosure without consequence. New matters should give us a termination right or an indemnity, not a cure.

Paragraph 1.4 (no admission of breach or materiality) is common. It is acceptable only if the general disclosure is narrowed. In combination with 1.1, it means the Seller discloses everything and admits nothing.

---

## 3. Buyer knowledge, Clause 8.3

This is probably the single most damaging clause. It bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". That is constructive knowledge. Combined with the general disclosure, it would remove most of our warranty protection for exactly the issues we have already found.

**Push back:**
- **Preferred:** a "pro-sandbagging" clause, so that the Buyer's knowledge does not affect claims.
- **Fallback:** an exclusion only for the **actual knowledge** of named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals. No advisers, no imputed or constructive knowledge, no "discoverable".
- In any case, knowledge must not affect the specific indemnities, the tax indemnity or title claims.

---

## 4. Specific issues

### 4.1 Bluefen consent: about 30% of FY26 revenue (Clause 3 / 6.3; DL para 2)
The Letter confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. The Seller offers only reasonable endeavours, and wants the condition "treated as satisfied" on delivery of any written consent, even if the 11.3 conditions remain open or the consent is conditional.

**Push back:**
- Make this a **condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit**, waivable only by the Buyer. It should require an unconditional (or Buyer-approved) written consent under clause 11.2, plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The consent should be in a form approved by the Buyer, and it should not change pricing or other terms of the Bluefen contract without our consent.
- Raise the endeavours standard to "all reasonable endeavours". Give the Buyer the right to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- Include a sunset date and a Buyer termination right.
- Consider a price mechanism, such as an escrow or earn-out on Bluefen retention, given the revenue concentration.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility: about AUD 3.2m (Clause 2 / 7; DL para 3)
"Release to be provided following Completion" is **inconsistent with the debt-free basis**. Change of control under clause 8.1 is likely triggered on Completion, which risks default or acceleration while the Company is in our hands.

**Push back:**
- The facility should be repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price**, through the funds flow, and treated as Debt.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - a payout letter that also confirms the release becomes effective on receipt;
  - an executed deed of release;
  - an undertaking or authority to remove PPSR registrations;
  - the return of any title documents.
- Confirm whether Riverlark's security extends to **the shares themselves** (a share mortgage or security from the Seller). If it does, that release is also a title matter (see 4.9).

### 4.3 DD-005 completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 (funds flow; DL para 5)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow. They are **Company liabilities triggered by the transaction**. If they are not deducted, we pay for them.

**Push back:**
- Treat them as Debt or Transaction Costs, deducted from the price **grossed up for on-costs**: PAYG withholding, employer superannuation (completion bonuses may well attract super guarantee, so confirm), payroll tax, and workers' compensation.
- Pay them through Company payroll at Completion, or fund them into a retention.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or misclassification.
- Ask the Seller for the full bonus documentation and recipient list. Confirm there are no other change-of-control or retention payments.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP: SOW3 Project Materials (Clause 11.1; DL para 4)
Under DD-004 clause 7.3, **title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid**. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and the Seller concedes this is not bank verification. There is **no receipt and no confirmatory assignment**. The Company may therefore not own IP it is selling us. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the AUD 180k invoice. It does not cover loss of the IP, injunction or rework risk, or third-party claims.

**Push back:**
- **Completion deliverables:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, with moral rights consents where relevant.
- Expand the indemnity to **all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or have the right to use, the SOW3 Project Materials**. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge limitations, with a long survival period.
- If assignment cannot be delivered before Completion, hold a specific retention.
- Find out how SOW3 materials are used in the product. If they are core, consider making the assignment a condition precedent.

### 4.5 DD-006 export and privacy incident: about 1,240 records (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL para 6)
The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Its own Letter says that access, scope and whether notification is required are **all unestablished**. Names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps are personal information.

Under the Privacy Act notifiable data breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within **30 days**. The incident was known by 22 September 2026, and we are now around six weeks past that date. The assessment may therefore already be overdue, which is a compliance issue in itself. Regulatory penalty exposure for serious privacy contraventions has also risen materially in recent years.

**Push back:**
- Require, before signing or as a condition precedent:
  - the completed assessment;
  - any forensic report;
  - the notification decision with reasons;
  - confirmation that the external recipient has deleted the material (attestation or log evidence);
  - confirmation of root cause and remediation.
- Add a **specific indemnity** covering regulatory investigations, penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims and lost contracts. It should sit outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge limitations, and survive for several years.
- Add a privacy and cybersecurity warranty, with no "not material" gloss.
- Assess whether any affected records belong to Bluefen or other key customers. That links back to the consent risk in 4.1.

### 4.6 Sandbar supplier renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 (DL para 8)
The Seller asserts these are "ordinary course", yet the Letter tells us to read them together for timing and scope. Three equal, related renewals look like a **split commitment**. It may have been structured to sit under an approval or material-contract threshold, or entered into close to sale.

**Questions for the Seller:**
- When were the renewals signed?
- Who approved them, and are they related-party?
- Are they terminable for convenience?
- Are they prepaid, accrued or unpaid?
- What is the Company's actual usage?

**Push back:**
- Warranty on ordinary course and material contracts, with aggregation of related contracts.
- Any unpaid committed amounts beyond ordinary run-rate should be treated as Debt.
- If they are related-party, treat them as leakage.
- Or require termination at the Seller's cost.

### 4.7 Office lease, DD-007 (DL para 7)
The Seller only says the material "does not describe" a consent requirement. That is not a statement that no consent is needed. Australian leases frequently deem a change in shareholding to be an assignment. **Our property counsel should review DD-007 independently.** At minimum:
- the notification should be a Completion deliverable;
- the Seller should warrant that the share sale gives the landlord no consent, termination or bond rights.

### 4.8 Mossvale, DD-009 (DL para 9)
This is the same drafting technique as the lease. An anti-assignment clause may extend to change of control. **We should review it independently.** If there is any doubt, seek a comfort letter or consent and include a warranty.

### 4.9 Title, DD-012 (DL para 10)
The register is prima facie evidence of title only. The Seller expressly says it does not confirm that we have verified title. **Push back:**
- **Fundamental title warranty:** sole legal and beneficial owner, free of Encumbrances, with no options, convertibles, ESOP or rights to issue shares. Cap at 100%, long survival (see 1.4).
- Our own ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - signed share transfers;
  - share certificates (or a lost certificate indemnity);
  - releases of any security over the shares (see the Riverlark point in 4.2);
  - Seller board approvals;
  - updated registers.

### 4.10 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Reject.** We need:
- a **stand-alone tax indemnity** for pre-Completion taxes, outside the cap and basket, with survival tied to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer;
- tax conduct-of-claims provisions;
- full IP warranties, with the Ironquay issue handled by the specific indemnity in 4.4.

---

## 5. Cash-free/debt-free mechanics
Make sure the Debt and Transaction Costs definitions expressly capture:
- the Riverlark facility, including break costs and interest to Completion;
- the DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs;
- accrued pre-Completion tax;
- Seller-side adviser fees borne by the Company;
- unpaid committed Sandbar amounts beyond the ordinary run-rate.

We should also check the treatment of deferred revenue in a SaaS business.

---

## 6. Security for claims
Given the unresolved items (Bluefen, the incident and Ironquay), propose the following:
- a **general escrow of around 10% of price** (AUD 2.4m) for 18–24 months; and/or
- **specific retentions** for the privacy incident and Ironquay until they are resolved; or
- W&I insurance for general warranties, with the known issues excluded from W&I and covered by Seller specific indemnities. W&I will not cover disclosed or known matters, which makes the specific indemnities essential.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Framing | Positions "[STANDARD]/FINAL", review only "[OPEN]" | Reject. Nothing agreed until all agreed; confirm internally what principals actually agreed |
| 2 | General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | 30–50%, or 20% only with W&I, escrow and carve-outs |
| 3 | Thresholds | AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k deductible basket | AUD 5–10k de minimis with aggregation; tipping basket at about 0.5% |
| 4 | Time limits | 18 months for all Claims | 18–24 months general only; tax 5–7 years; title 7 years; indemnities tailored |
| 5 | Fundamentals | Same cap and time as general | 100% cap, no thresholds, long survival |
| 6 | Limitations/non-reliance | Apply to all Claims | Carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, title and covenants |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; no disclosure against indemnities; no cure by update |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Actual and constructive, including advisers | Pro-sandbagging; fallback is actual knowledge of named individuals only |
| 9 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; "deemed satisfied" | Buyer-only condition precedent including 11.3 conditions; sunset and termination right; consider escrow |
| 10 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Repay from proceeds at Completion; payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge as deliverables |
| 11 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Omitted from funds flow | Deduct as Debt grossed up for super, payroll tax and PAYG; specific indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment evidence and confirmatory assignment at Completion; full IP-loss indemnity outside limits; retention |
| 13 | Privacy incident | "Not expected to be material" | Completed NDB assessment and forensics now; specific indemnity outside limits; retention |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Diligence the split; aggregation warranty; Debt or leakage treatment, or termination |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Read as no consent required | Independent review; notices or comfort letters; warranty |
| 16 | Title | Register only | Fundamental warranty; our own ASIC/PPSR searches; full Completion deliverables |
| 17 | Tax / IP | General regime | Stand-alone tax indemnity; full IP warranties |

**Priority for the mark-up:**
1. Reject the disclosure and knowledge architecture (sections 2 and 3). It undermines everything else.
2. Fix the Debt items (Riverlark and bonuses) in the funds flow.
3. Make Bluefen a true Buyer condition precedent.
4. Obtain specific indemnities with retention for the privacy incident and Ironquay.
5. Carve fundamentals, tax and fraud out of the limitation package.

*This analysis is a structured first review for the deal team. NSW/Australian counsel should confirm the points of law before the mark-up goes out, in particular the privacy NDB timing, super and payroll tax on the bonuses, tax limitation periods, and the lease change-of-control treatment.*
=== END ADVICE ===
